result.output:
# Windows GUI test VM (GCP) — working harness

Drives a wxWidgets + OpenGL desktop app on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP,
headlessly: launch it, screenshot it, click it, verify the result.

Verified 2026-09-07 with OrcaSlicer 2.4.2 portable.

## The VM

    instance : jusprin-win-test
    project  : elegoo-backend
    zone     : us-central1-a
    machine  : n2-standard-8, Windows Server 2022, 100GB pd-balanced
    display  : virtual display device ENABLED (required, see below)
    login    : ssh as guitest with ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine

The external IP is ephemeral and CHANGES on every stop/start. Re-read it with:

    gcloud compute instances describe jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a \
      --project=elegoo-backend \
      --format="value(networkInterfaces[0].accessConfigs[0].natIP)"

then update winssh.sh / winscp.sh.

## Four things that had to be solved

1. **OpenGL.** The app hard-requires OpenGL 3.2 (src/slic3r/GUI/OpenGLManager.cpp)
   and exits below it. Stock Windows software rendering reports 1.1. Fix: drop
   Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (from pal1000/mesa-dist-win) next
   to the .exe. Reports OpenGL 4.2 on plain CPU.

   Mesa then auto-picks its **d3d12** backend, because the GCE virtual display
   exposes "Microsoft Basic Render Driver" as a D3D12 device — and that path
   crashed on the first frame. run-app.cmd forces the CPU rasterizer with
   `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`.

   Do NOT copy the whole Mesa .7z onto the VM: Windows Defender flags the archive
   as Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn and deletes it. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere and
   copy just those — Defender does not object to them, so no AV exclusion is
   needed. (The archive's sha256 matches GitHub's published release digest; the
   detection is a heuristic on the bundle, which also contains Vulkan layers,
   D3D12 compilers and media-foundation encoders we don't use.)

2. **A visible desktop.** A GUI app started from an SSH shell lands in a session
   with no desktop and screenshots come back black. autologon.ps1 creates a local
   admin `guitest` and sets Winlogon AutoAdminLogon so console session 1 is always
   live. Something in the GCE image clears those values after the boot that sets
   them, so startup.ps1 re-applies them on EVERY boot.

3. **Session isolation.** Display APIs, EnumWindows and Get-Process MainWindowTitle
   only see the CALLING session's window station. Run them over SSH and they
   silently report nothing — which reads as "the app has no window" when it does.
   Everything that touches the UI goes through `Invoke-InSession` in harness.ps1,
   which registers a scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive` so it runs in
   session 1, and writes its output to a file to be read back over SSH.

4. **Resolution.** Without a GCE virtual display device the guest falls back to
   Microsoft Basic Display Adapter with no EDID = 640x480, and the app's own
   window is 760x500. Fix (requires the instance to be STOPPED):

       gcloud compute instances stop   jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend
       gcloud compute instances update jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend --enable-display-device
       gcloud compute instances start  jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend

   Then 1920x1080 is available via set-res.ps1.

## Also required by this app

Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime is NOT present on a clean Windows Server image.
Without it the app puts up a modal "WebView2 Runtime" prompt and startup blocks
forever. Installed here as 152.0.4191.66 via the Evergreen bootstrapper:

    Invoke-WebRequest "https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?LinkId=2124703" -OutFile setup.exe
    .\setup.exe /silent /install

This matters more for JusPrin than for stock Orca, since JusPrin's UI is
WebView-based.

## Files

    startup.ps1      GCE windows-startup-script-ps1: OpenSSH, port 22 firewall,
                     authorized_keys, calls autologon.ps1. Runs every boot.
    autologon.ps1    Creates guitest + sets AutoAdminLogon. Idempotent.
    harness.ps1      Invoke-InSession / Take-Screenshot. Source this first.
    screenshot.ps1   Screen capture. Must run in-session.
    probe.ps1        Lists session 1's real windows to C:\guitest\windows.txt.
    focus-app.ps1    Closes leftover task consoles, maximizes the app window.
    click.ps1        Clicks the "x,y" in C:\guitest\click.txt.
    set-res.ps1      Sets 1920x1080. Must run in-session.
    install-app.ps1  Downloads the app, places the Mesa DLLs beside the .exe.
    run-app.cmd      Launches the app with llvmpipe forced, detached.
    winssh.sh        ssh wrapper. winscp.sh: scp wrapper.

## Typical cycle

    ./winscp.sh <local.ps1> guitest@<IP>:C:/guitest/
    ./winssh.sh '. C:\guitest\harness.ps1; Invoke-InSession -TaskName "X" ...'
    ./winssh.sh '. C:\guitest\harness.ps1; Take-Screenshot'
    ./winscp.sh guitest@<IP>:C:/guitest/shot.png ./shot.png

## Known gap

There is no current JusPrin Windows binary to test. The Build all workflow's
Windows job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with "could not find any
instance of Visual Studio"; last green Windows build was 2026-03-04 and its
artifacts have expired. Either fix that job, or install VS Build Tools on this VM
and build from the cached OrcaSlicer_dep_win64 artifact.
---
name: windows-gui-test-vm-gcp
description: Working recipe for testing the OrcaSlicer/JusPrin GUI headlessly on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP, and the four traps that make it fail silently.
metadata:
  type: project
---

A Windows GUI test VM for this app works in GCP with no GPU. Instance
`jusprin-win-test`, project `elegoo-backend`, zone `us-central1-a`,
n2-standard-16 (16 vCPU, 64 GB, Cascade Lake), 500 GB pd-balanced,
Windows Server 2022. Harness + full README live outside the repo
at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/vm-harness/windows/`. Verified 2026-09-07 end to end:
launch, screenshot, scripted click, verify the UI advanced.

**Why:** four failure modes here are silent — they look like "the app has no
window" or "the app hung" rather than reporting an error, so they cost hours if
rediscovered from scratch.

**How to apply:**
- OpenGL: the app hard-requires 3.2 and Windows software rendering is 1.1. Drop
  Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` beside the .exe. Then force
  `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` — otherwise Mesa picks
  its d3d12 backend (the GCE virtual display exposes a D3D12 device) and crashes
  on the first frame.
- Never copy the whole Mesa .7z to the VM: Defender deletes it as
  Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere, copy only those, and
  no AV exclusion is needed.
- Session isolation is the big one: display APIs, EnumWindows and
  MainWindowTitle only see the calling session's window station, so over SSH they
  report nothing and it reads as "no window exists". Run anything UI-touching as a
  scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive`.
- Auto-logon must be re-applied on every boot; the GCE image clears the Winlogon
  values after the boot that sets them.
- Resolution needs `gcloud compute instances update --enable-display-device`
  (instance must be stopped) or you get 640x480, smaller than the app's own window.
- WebView2 runtime is absent on a clean Windows Server image; without it the app
  blocks on a modal prompt at startup. Matters especially for JusPrin's
  WebView-based UI. See [[jusprin-rebrand-seams]].

Claude Code and the Claude desktop app are both installed for `guitest`
(2026-09-08). CLI: the native Windows installer `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1`
puts `claude.exe` in `C:\Users\guitest\.local\bin` - no Node needed, the box has
none. Desktop app: install with Anthropic's own Intune script,
`https://downloads.claude.ai/releases/enterprise/intune/Install-Claude.ps1 -Scope User`,
which resolves the official MSIX and verifies its signature and publisher identity.
MSIX deployment works on this Windows Server 2022 image. Launch the packaged app in
session 1 through explorer.exe, so it lands at normal integrity even though the
scheduled task is elevated:
`Invoke-InSession -Exe C:\Windows\explorer.exe -ArgLine "shell:AppsFolder\Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc!Claude"`.
Electron renders fine on this GPU-less VM with no flags.

RDP: port 3389 is open project-wide via `default-allow-rdp` (to 0.0.0.0/0 - not
narrowed yet), and RDP as `guitest` reconnects to the existing console session
rather than starting a second one. Run `./get-rdp-password.sh` in the harness to
print the current credentials; it resolves the ephemeral IP itself and verifies
the password actually authenticates before handing it to you. Do NOT use
`gcloud compute reset-windows-password` - autologon.ps1 re-syncs the account to
Winlogon\DefaultPassword at the next boot and would undo it.

autologon.ps1 used to mint a NEW random password on every boot, so any reboot
silently invalidated the RDP credentials. Fixed 2026-09-09: it now reuses the
stored DefaultPassword and only generates one when that value is absent (delete
the value and reboot to rotate deliberately). This matters because Windows
Update on this VM is set to install and restart on its own, daily at 3 AM, and
the box has also rebooted unexpectedly several times - Kernel-Power event 41,
cause not established.

Two mechanical traps: nested quoting through `winssh.sh` into `powershell -Command`
mangles almost anything non-trivial - write a .ps1, scp it, run it with `-File`.
And a PATH change made over SSH does not reach session 1's already-running Explorer;
re-set the variable from inside the session and restart Explorer, or a new terminal
there still will not find the command.

Tuned 2026-09-08, both changes measured. Windows Defender had real-time scanning
on with zero exclusions, so it scanned every object file the compiler wrote.
Excluding C:\src, C:\tools, C:\guitest plus the compiler binaries took a
small-file write benchmark from 545 to 983 files/s and reads from 979 to 2257 -
roughly 1.8x and 2.3x, for free. Re-add these if the VM is ever rebuilt.

The boot disk was grown 100 -> 500 GB. On GCE a balanced persistent disk's speed
scales with its provisioned size (140 MB/s + 0.28 per GB), so the old 100 GB disk
was capped at 168 MB/s - it was slow *because* it was small. Aggregate write went
from that 168 ceiling to a measured 262 MB/s. Resize is online: `gcloud compute
disks resize`, then `Resize-Partition` on disk 0 partition 3; C: is the last
partition so nothing blocks the extend, and no reboot is needed.

**Do not benchmark GCE persistent disk with one synchronous writer.** A single
WriteThrough stream is latency-bound and reported only 185 MB/s on the 500 GB
disk, which reads as 'the resize did nothing'. Eight concurrent writers showed the
real 262 MB/s. Use concurrent writers - that is also what a parallel build does.

RDP now prefers the H.264 codec: AVC444ModePreferred=1 (DWORD) under
HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services, effective on the
next connection. That does not touch the real interactivity limit, which is the
~57 ms round-trip from California to us-central1; only moving the VM to a west
coast region fixes that.

The external IP is ephemeral and changes on every stop/start.

content.text:
The mobile webcam fix is landed on TSDApp master as one commit, `d8ab34b7`, and pushed. In Sentry, OBICO-MOBILE-24W is resolved for the next release, anchored to Android 2.43+337, the release that's out now. If a later build crashes this way again, Sentry reopens it as a regression. Its email is in Trash. Jest ran 16 of 16 tests passing. The one test file that failed to load, `__tests__/App-test.js`, also fails on the commit before mine, so it was already broken.

I moved on to the next issues: the JusPrin crash after dividing an object, and the save failure that followed it. I've diagnosed both from the code, but I haven't reproduced either, so per your rule I haven't fixed them. I posted the findings on both Sentry issues.

**The divide crash (JUSPRIN-APP-J) is Windows and Linux only.**
- Splitting an object deletes the original from the model and adds the pieces.
- On Windows and Linux, adding each piece to the object list immediately selects it in the 3D view. That happens before the 3D scene is rebuilt, so the selection reads a model object by an index that has just gone stale, and that read hits garbage memory.
- The macOS build skips that selection step (it sits in `#ifndef __WXOSX__` in `GUI_ObjectList.cpp`), so it can't crash on a Mac. Reproducing it needs a Windows build on the `jusprin-win-test` VM.
- One thing I can't explain yet: why the Cut tool in the normal interface, which uses the same function, doesn't crash the same way.

**The save failure (JUSPRIN-APP-K) is probably caused by those crashes.**
- Every assistant action gets a number such as `t-12`. The counter lives in the project state file, which is saved later. The record of each action is written to disk at once.
- If the app dies between those two writes, the next run hands out `t-12` again. Writing that record fails with "operation version record already exists", and the person is told the project wasn't saved.
- This user had just crashed three times, which fits. This hypothesis can be tested on this Mac: run an assistant action, kill the app, restart it, and run another.

**Decision needed: which of the two to reproduce first.**
- **Save failure first, on this Mac (my pick).** It costs nothing extra, it's quick, and it protects everyone, because any crash or forced quit sets up the same failure.
- **The divide crash.** It needs a JusPrin build on the shared Windows VM, which takes a long time and slows down the other sessions building there. Then I'd have to drive a divide through the assistant on the VM.

Should I reproduce the save failure on this Mac first, or do both now?
check with the eorro handling session to see if this can be one of the issues it has handled

input.summary: Ask whether two JusPrin Sentry issues are already handled
input.message:
Question from the Sentry inbox triage session: are either of these two JusPrin 2.0.1 Sentry issues already covered by the error-handling work you've done (or a commit on jusprin-dev)? Please reply with facts only (commit hashes, or "not covered"); don't change Sentry.

1) JUSPRIN-APP-K, 2026-11-26 11:55 UTC, Windows, one user: ToolCallFailure "local_save_failed: The change was made, but the project could not be saved: operation version record already exists." Raised by `require(!fs::exists(file), ...)` in `ProjectVersionStore::record_operation` (ProjectVersionStore.cpp ~line 962), after `object_divide`. My hypothesis (not reproduced): action ids come from `ProjectStateDocument::allocate_action_id()` (`counters.nextAction`, saved later with the document), while `record_operation` writes `operations/<id>.json` at once. If the app dies between the two, the next run reissues the same t-N and the record collides. This user's app had just crashed three times. Question: did you already change how action ids are allocated or persisted, or how record_operation treats an existing record? Or is this only about how the failure is shown (your D5, "local_save_failed stays a failure even when the change ran")?

2) JUSPRIN-APP-J (G and H merged into it), same user, three crashes 11:49-11:53 UTC: EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION_READ in `Selection::get_bounding_box_in_reference_system`, reached from `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::divide_object` (OrcaReshape.cpp:244) → `Plater::apply_cut_object_to_model` → `load_model_objects` → `ObjectList::add_object_to_list` → `selection_changed` (the `#ifndef __WXOSX__` block, so Windows/Linux only) → canvas selection read with stale object indices before `update()` reloads the scene. Have you touched divide_object, apply_cut_object_to_model, or this crash?

input.recap: I asked the JusPrin error-handling session whether it already covers the divide crash or the save failure, and it hasn't replied yet. Its latest commit on jusprin-dev, e895b0d065, changes only who gets told when a save fails, not why this one fails.

content.text:
I sent the error-handling session ([Handoff error handling](#local_2bc65560-8e6d-4551-9a47-d99179fc6145)) both issues, with the details. It's in the middle of another turn, so the message is queued and it hasn't answered yet. I'll pass its answer on when it arrives.

Meanwhile I checked the JusPrin history myself.

- **Save failure (JUSPRIN-APP-K):** that session's latest commit on jusprin-dev, `e895b0d065` from today, changes who is told when a save fails. If the operating system refuses the save, for example a full disk or a read-only folder, the person sees the system's reason and nothing is reported to us. Any other save failure is reported to us. Our failure doesn't come from the operating system: JusPrin's own "record already exists" check raises it. So after that commit it would still be reported to us, and nothing there stops the operation number from being reused after a crash. Its transcript mentions this error only in a design note, "local_save_failed stays a failure even when the change ran". That note is about how the failure is shown, not its cause.
- **Divide crash (JUSPRIN-APP-J):** I found no commit since November 18 that touches the divide function, the cut-and-replace function in the 3D view, or the selection code it crashes in. No transcript of any session mentions this crash path either.

So far, neither issue looks handled. The session's own answer will settle it.
Reproduce on the mac first.

content.text:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.


Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - **Original request:** "Find all Sentry issues in my inbox. check with the session who have triaged some of these to get the updates. Then triage the rest yourself. afterwards. Tell me what issues need to be addressed". This is done.
   - **Pushback on the mobile fix:** the user asked whether the OBICO-MOBILE-24W fix and its explanation were right, or whether the fix was in the wrong place. Investigated; the root cause was corrected.
   - **"shared method or function … go ahead and do it. And also, check obico-server build front end to see if may have the same problem."** Done.
   - **"Land it on master as one commit. marked the Sentry issue as resolved in the next release, and delete email from the inbox. Move on to the next issue."** Landed, resolved and trashed. Moved on to the JusPrin divide crash (JUSPRIN-APP-J) and the save failure (JUSPRIN-APP-K).
   - **"check with the eorro handling session to see if this can be one of the issues it has handled"** Message sent; no reply yet.
   - **Current request: "Reproduce on the mac first."** That is, reproduce the JUSPRIN-APP-K save failure ("operation version record already exists") on macOS before fixing anything.

   Standing constraints from CLAUDE.md and memory, preserved:
   - Use `gcloud config set account ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com` before any gcloud or kubectl command. The personal account `k@obico.io` is reserved for the user.
   - Sentry API base is `https://sentry.obico.io/api/0/`, with the token in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Every note must start with `**By Claude Code** — `.
   - "Never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce." Reproduce in local dev first, and show the broken behavior before the fix and the correct behavior after it.
   - Never commit or stage submodule updates.
   - Before committing, review `git status` and `git diff`. Ask for confirmation before any revert, reset or amend.
   - Report outcomes, not the journey. Use full sentences with no invented labels. Start decisions with "Decision needed".
   - The user can't see the next-step box, so every question has to be written out in full in the message.
   - Use gog for Gmail, run outside the sandbox; never print credentials.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Sentry triage workflow:**
     - Merges are done in the browser through Claude in Chrome, then checked on the Merged Issues tab.
     - Resolving with inNextRelease anchors to the project's latest release.
     - Noise is ignored with ignoreCount/ignoreWindow, or ignoreUserCount when there are real users.
     - The email sync checks each issue with the shortids lookup.
   - **React Native (TSDApp):**
     - useSelector with Redux.
     - Optional chaining short-circuits: the crash needs `webcamOpts[printerId]` to exist, meaning the person once saved a rotation.
     - A custom hook is just a shared function whose name starts with `use` and which calls useSelector.
     - Tests use Jest with react-test-renderer.
   - **moonraker-obico** reports `webcams=[]` when streaming fails with any exception other than JanusNotFound, or when every webcam is disabled. Both agents always mark exactly one webcam primary.
   - **JusPrin divide crash (C++, wxWidgets, OrcaSlicer fork), Windows/Linux only:**
     1. Plater::apply_cut_object_to_model deletes the object.
     2. load_model_objects runs.
     3. ObjectList::add_object_to_list runs; its `#ifndef __WXOSX__` block calls Select and selection_changed.
     4. update_selections_on_canvas runs before update() reloads the scene.
     5. Selection::get_bounding_box_in_reference_system reads `m_model->objects[vol.object_idx()]` with a stale index.
   - **JusPrin save-failure mechanism (JUSPRIN-APP-K):**
     - ProjectStateDocument::allocate_action_id() keeps `counters.nextAction` in the document, in memory.
     - ProjectVersionStore::record_operation writes `operations/<action_id>.json` immediately and calls `require(!fs::exists(file), "operation version record already exists")`.
     - In a model turn, ShellController calls record_agent_operation with `save = !in_model_turn()`, which is false, so the document is saved only at the end of the turn.
     - A crash mid-turn therefore leaves records numbered ahead of the persisted counter. After a restart the same t-N is issued again and the record collides.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - **TSDApp, new file `src/hooks/usePrimaryWebcam.js`** (committed in d8ab34b7):
     ```js
     import _ from 'lodash';
     import {useSelector} from 'react-redux';
     export const selectPrimaryWebcam = (state, printerId) => {
       const webcams = _.find(state.printers, {id: printerId})?.settings?.webcams;
       if (webcams && webcams.length === 1) { return webcams[0]; }
       return _.find(webcams, {is_primary_camera: true});
     };
     export const selectWebcamUserRotationDeg = (state, printerId, webcam) => {
       if (!webcam) { return 0; }
       return state.preferences?.webcamOpts?.[printerId.toString()]?.[webcam.name]?.userRotationDeg || 0;
     };
     const usePrimaryWebcam = (printerId) => {
       const primaryWebcam = useSelector((state) => selectPrimaryWebcam(state, printerId));
       const userRotationDeg = useSelector((state) => selectWebcamUserRotationDeg(state, printerId, primaryWebcam));
       return {primaryWebcam, userRotationDeg};
     };
     export default usePrimaryWebcam;
     ```
   - **TSDApp, changed screens.** PrinterItem.js, PrinterCard.js and PrinterControls.js now use:
     ```js
     const {primaryWebcam, userRotationDeg: webcamUserRotationDeg} = usePrimaryWebcam(printerId);
     ```
     FullScreenWebCam.js now uses:
     ```js
     useSelector((state) => webcam || selectPrimaryWebcam(state, printerId))
     ```
     and `selectWebcamUserRotationDeg`.
   - **TSDApp, new tests:**
     - `src/screens/Printer/__tests__/PrinterControls-test.js` renders the screen with `webcams: []` and a saved rotation. It failed before the fix with the Sentry TypeError at PrinterControls.js:34.
     - `src/hooks/__tests__/usePrimaryWebcam-test.js` covers the selectors.
   - **Commit:** "Printer screens no longer crash for a printer that reports no webcam", d8ab34b7 on master, pushed to origin.
     - 16 of 16 tests pass.
     - `__tests__/App-test.js` fails to load because of RNGestureHandlerModule. It failed the same way on 709adbff.
   - **devops/.claude/skills/sentry-triage/references/duplicate-patterns.md:** appended a "2026-11-26 inbox triage addendum". The file already had other uncommitted changes, and none of it is committed.
   - **Sentry-triage logs:** appended entries to `state/sentry-triage-run-log.jsonl` and `state/sentry-email-checks.jsonl`.
   - **JusPrin files read, no changes:**
     - `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaReshape.cpp`: divide_object, line 244 calls apply_cut_object_to_model.
     - `src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp`: apply_cut_object_to_model at line 19692; load_model_objects at about line 10477.
     - `src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_ObjectList.cpp`: the `#ifndef __WXOSX__` select block and selection_changed.
     - `src/slic3r/GUI/Selection.cpp`: around line 1166.
     - `src/slic3r/GUI/Gizmos/GLGizmoCut.cpp`: perform_cut.
     - `ProjectVersionStore.cpp`: record_operation at about line 952.
     - `ProjectAutosave.cpp`: record_agent_operation at about line 1177; save_now at line 1105.
     - `ProjectStateDocument.cpp`: allocate_action_id at line 980.
     - `ShellController.cpp`: about lines 726-745 (in_model_turn and the version callbacks).
     - `Agent/ProjectPersistence.hpp/.cpp`: flush is a no-op in managed mode; ProjectAutosave publishes the document.
     - `.claude/vm-harness/windows/README.md`: the Windows VM jusprin-win-test harness.

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **kubectl Django shell failed** with ModuleNotFoundError settings_ent. Fixed by running in `/web_ent` with `-c tsdweb-prod` and `SENTRY_DSN=` empty.
   - **zsh glob error with `--include=*.js`:** dropped the include patterns.
   - **grep over static_build produced 7 MB of output:** excluded static_build.
   - **The git push ran even though Jest had reported a failing suite** (I chained the commands). I checked afterwards: App-test fails the same way on the previous commit, so nothing new was broken.
   - **wrap_up rejected the commit action** because none was available; I re-called it without the action.
   - **User feedback:** the user challenged the "several webcams, none primary" explanation. I had repeated the previous commit's claim without checking it. I corrected it with production data and posted a correction note on Sentry 2131.

5. Problem Solving:
   - **Inbox triage is complete.** Seven Sentry inbox emails were left; one of them (24W) has since been fixed and trashed.
   - Six remain:
     - JUSPRIN-APP-K
     - JUSPRIN-APP-J
     - OBICO-SERVER-B2B, in two emails: the issue and a regression notice. It is Kenny's own traffic; the open question is whether real JusPrin 1 customers get refused on jusprinv2.obico.io/ent/jusprin/v2/web/jusprin1.
     - OBICO-SERVER-B2V: `notify` bool `.lower()` at api/octoprint_views.py:413; not fixed.
     - WHISPRNOTES-APP-5P: Singular SDK clipboard hang.
   - **JUSPRIN-APP-J** is Windows-only and needs the jusprin-win-test VM to reproduce. The Cut gizmo's use of the same function not crashing is still unexplained.
   - **JUSPRIN-APP-K** mechanism is identified from the code but not yet reproduced.
   - **Other session messages:** the tunnel-fix session mentioned that OBICO-SERVER-B26 may rise now that TUNNEL_DOMAIN has been removed from production.

6. All user messages:
   - "Find all Sentry issues in my inbox. check with the session who have triaged some of these to get the updates. Then triage the rest yourself. afterwards. Tell me what issues need to be addressed"
   - Quoted my item 1 (the Android 2.43 crash): "This got me worried. Are you sure this is going to be the final text? Because it sounds like the previous agents did a lousy job at fixing a bug. Or maybe we're barking up the wrong tree. Maybe that's the wrong place to fix the bug because it's not the root cause."
   - "By shared hook, you mean shared method or function, right? are you really talking about a callback hook or something? If it's a shared method or function, it makes sense, go ahead and do it. And also, check obico-server build front end to see if may have the same problem."
   - "Land it on master as one commit. marked the Sentry issue as resolved in the next release, and delete email from the inbox. Move on to the next issue."
   - "check with the eorro handling session to see if this can be one of the issues it has handled"
   - "Reproduce on the mac first."
   - The cross-session messages from the Release 2.0.2, Security sweep and Fix-six-urgent sessions came from other Claude sessions, not from the user.

7. Pending Tasks:
   - Reproduce JUSPRIN-APP-K (the save failure) on the Mac. Only after reproducing it, propose or implement a fix.
   - Watch for the reply from the "Handoff error handling" session, local_2bc65560-8e6d-4551-9a47-d99179fc6145, about whether J or K is already covered, and pass it on to the user.
   - JUSPRIN-APP-J needs a Windows reproduction on jusprin-win-test. It comes after K, and its cost has to be raised with the user.
   - The remaining open inbox issues (B2B, B2V, WHISPRNOTES-APP-5P) haven't been started.

8. Current Work:
   I was reproducing JUSPRIN-APP-K on macOS. The confirmed mechanism, from ShellController.cpp:
   ```cpp
   const auto in_model_turn = [this] { return m_agent_pane && m_agent_pane->web_view().host().busy(); };
   ...
   m_autosave->record_agent_operation(activity.action_id, activity.tool, outcome, before, !in_model_turn());
   ```
   And from ProjectAutosave::record_agent_operation:
   ```cpp
   saved = save && save_now();
   if (!before.empty()) m_store->record_operation(action_id, tool, outcome, before, saved ? m_committed_head : std::string());
   ```
   - In a chat turn, save is false, so `operations/t-N.json` is written but `counters.nextAction` is not persisted until the turn ends. An MCP or external edit outside a turn saves first, so it would not reproduce the bug.
   - The code is present in jusprin/v2.0.0 and v2.0.1.
   - Environment:
     - /Applications/JusPrin.app is 2.0.0 (io.obico.jusprin). Its data is in ~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2, and JusPrin2-stg also exists.
     - The dev build at /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/OrcaSlicer.app is from Nov 12.
     - No JusPrin app is running; two jusprin-mcp processes are.
     - The jusprin-ci runner is building the release on this Mac.
     - The main JusPrin checkout (branch jusprin-dev) is used by other sessions, so read only there and use a worktree for any changes.
   - Env hooks found: JUSPRIN_SERVER_URL, JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL, JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL, JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN. There's no scripted AI provider.
   - Last step: grepped JusPrin CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and tests for test-account, staging or chat-test guidance; nothing matched. Earlier, the Release session had said a chat test needs a JusPrin test account, or Kenny signing in.

9. Optional Next Step:

description: "Drive the real app signed in to a local gateway through an injected page script; which conf keys, why a copied binary dies, and what still needs the screen."
metadata:

Builds on [[live-host-check-via-instrumented-dev-page]]; used 2026-11-02 when screen control of the app was denied.

- Signed-in conf needs all of: `jusprin_agent.{provider=jusprin, jusprin_api_key, enabled=true, cloud_consent=true, jusprin_model_formats=<JSON id→format from GET /ent/jusprin/v2/models>}`, `jusprin_server.base_url`, `jusprin_onboarding.status=completed`. Without the formats the Agent says "not set up".
- An installed printer is `"models":[{"vendor":"Custom","model":"Generic Klipper Printer","nozzle_diameter":"0.4"}]`, not `vendors`.
- Kill the app before editing the conf. Replace a scratch binary with `rm` then `cp`: `cp` over a binary that has run gets the new process killed at launch.
- `Contents/Resources` in the build is a symlink to the worktree. Replace it with a real folder of links before corrupting a resource, or the worktree gets corrupted.
- Bringing the app forward triggers an account refresh, so to race the gateway (a real 402), change the ledger and send without refocusing.
- Page text input: native value setter plus an `input` event. A modal Preferences window's page polls as `agent-preferences`.
- A test preset needs a `version` field or import rejects it.
- A compose recreate drops env set by a wrapper; check `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES` before any chat so only the fake upstream is reachable.

Still needs the screen: pointer hover, native file dialogs, Orca's wizard.
=== live-test-built-app-on-mac.md
---
name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.

---
name: model-probe-live-chat-harness
description: "Scripted live in-app chat test: shell harness --model-probe mode (uncommitted, branch claude/model-nature-probe), file-driven turns, about 90k tokens per 2-turn conversation; Thingiverse files only download through the built-in browser."
metadata:

---

On 2026-10-12 I added `--model-probe <model> <exchange-dir>` to `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` in the worktree `.claude/worktrees/model-nature-probe` (branch `claude/model-nature-probe`, cut from jusprin-newui d0bce03db3, **uncommitted**; Release build, about 15 minutes for `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs shell_integration_harness`). It loads one model into a clean project with the live Agent, writes `turn-N.json` (conversation, every tool call with arguments and result, pictures as `.b64`) once the chat has been quiet for 8 s, then waits for `next-N.txt` holding the next user message or `END`. The run script and viewer were `run_probe.sh` and `show_turn.py` in that session's scratchpad; the key comes from `JusPrin2.conf` through `OPENAI_API_KEY`, with a scratch `$HOME` per run.

Measured cost on gpt-5.4-mini: 3 conversations (file-load message plus 2 user turns each) were 31 requests and 267,803 tokens, 82% of the input cached. Real tool results, no canned replies, so it fits [[prompt-eval-spend-budget]].

=== scratch-app-driving-traps.md
---
name: scratch-app-driving-traps
description: "Traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control: in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args and @import failures, the model picker needs page JS, a debugger attach once hung a slice."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439
  modified: 2026-11-12T18:04:04.144Z
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **`@import AppKit` can fail silently in lldb `expr`** ("no known method '-windows'"). Then cast everything to `id` and get classes with `((Class(*)(const char*))objc_getClass)("NSApplication")`; a working runner that runs a JS file in the chat panel (title "JusPrin Agent") was `runjs.sh` in the 2026-11-12 scratchpad.
- **The composer's model picker is a drop-down the background `app_click` refuses.** Click it from page JS via the runner above. OpenRouter's list labels models "Anthropic: Claude …", so a regex on "Claude Fable" picks OpenRouter's copy; the Anthropic-key one starts with "Claude".
- **A slice right after lldb attaches hung once (2026-11-12).** The worker sat in upstream `name_tbb_thread_pool_threads_set_locale()`, a barrier every TBB thread must reach, and the main thread waited in `BackgroundSlicingProcess::start()` forever. After a relaunch with no debugger the same slice ran at once. Suspected trigger: pausing the app while its thread pool was starting. Don't report such a hang as an app bug without a run that had no debugger attached.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

content.text:
I reproduced the JusPrin save failure (Sentry JUSPRIN-APP-K) on the Mac, with the same error text as the Windows report. It's a follow-on from the Windows divide crash (JUSPRIN-APP-J): if the app dies partway through a chat turn, the first edit after a restart can't be saved. I haven't written a fix yet.

**What happened to the Windows user.** It was one person, on 2.0.1:
- They hit the divide crash three times, at 11:49, 11:51 and 11:53.
- In the last crashed chat turn, the assistant ran two divide previews, then a divide that was logged as succeeded, and the app crashed one second later.
- They restarted at 11:53:47, reopened the project and asked for another cut. That divide failed with "operation version record already exists".

**Why it fails.** Every tool call gets a number from a counter kept in the project's document (t-1, t-2, …).
- An edit that changes the model also writes a small record file named after its number, such as `operations/t-4.json`.
- Inside a chat turn, only the first edit saves the project. Later edits write their record but leave the save to the end of the turn.
- The document, which holds the counter, reaches disk only after about 1.5 seconds without edits.
- If the app dies in that gap, the record file exists but the saved counter is still behind it.
- After a restart, the next call reuses the same number. If that call is an edit, its record collides with the leftover file, and the app refuses to save.

**How I reproduced it.** I used a copy of the installed 2.0.0 app with a scratch copy of the data folder:
1. I opened a 20 mm cube and sent a real chat message, on your account, asking for two separate cuts.
2. A watcher killed the app the moment the second cut's record (`t-4.json`) appeared. The saved document still said the next number was 4.
3. I relaunched, reopened the project, and asked in chat for one more cut. The assistant called the divide as its first tool, so it got t-4 again.
4. The assistant replied "I made the cut, but the project could not be saved." The log has the same error as Sentry: `object_divide (agent, t-4): local_save_failed: The change was made, but the project could not be saved: operation version record already exists.`

Only that one edit fails: the counter has moved on, so the next edit saves normally. The cuts from the crashed turn are lost, which is expected after a crash.

A crash isn't required. Force-quitting the app, a power cut or a lost battery during a chat turn would leave the same state. Fixing the Windows divide crash removes the most common trigger, but not this bug.

**Proposed fix (not done).** When a project opens, move the counter past the highest record number already in its operations folder. That covers every way the counter can fall behind. The other option is to save the document after every edit inside a chat turn. That only closes the gap for future crashes, and it costs a disk write per edit.

**Still open:**
- The error-handling session hasn't answered whether it already covers this issue.
- The scratch app copy and data folder are still in the session scratchpad. The data folder includes your sign-in key, so I'll delete it once the fix is verified.

content.text:
You're right to be worried. The failure comes from bookkeeping that almost nothing uses, and the error it raises is false. I've dropped my earlier proposal to adjust the counter when a project opens, because it would add a repair step on top of the same design.

**What the code does today (checked on v2.0.1 and jusprin-dev):**
- Every tool call takes a number from a counter stored in the project's document. When an edit finishes, the app writes a small file named after that number, such as `operations/t-4.json`. The file says which saved version the edit started from and which one it produced.
- The only code that reads these files is the cleanup that deletes old versions. It skips any version a record mentions. Nothing shows them to the person, and nothing uses them for undo or restore.
- Before writing a record, the app requires that no file with that name exists yet. If one does, the whole tool call reports "the project could not be saved".

**The problem.** The record's file name comes from a counter that lives in a different file and is written at a different time. When the two get out of step, two edits get the same number, and the existence check turns that into a save failure. That has now happened twice:
- In October, the printer panel restarted its numbers at t-1 each time it opened. That was fixed by sharing the project's counter.
- Now, a crash in the middle of a chat turn leaves a record on disk that the saved counter hasn't caught up with.

The October investigation also noted a third way in: if a project document is corrupt, it reloads with the counter back at 1 while the old records stay on disk.

**The error is false.** I checked the project from the reproduction after the "could not be saved" reply. Four seconds later, at the end of the turn, the app saved a new version with the cut in it. The project was saved; only the bookkeeping file wasn't written. So the person was told something untrue, the assistant warned them not to treat the project as saved, and Sentry got a report.

**Decision needed: what to do with the per-edit record files?** This is your call, because it depends on whether you planned a feature that reads them (for example, "undo this AI change"). I couldn't find one in the code or in my notes.
- **Remove them entirely.** Delete the record writing and the cleanup check that reads them. The cleanup would then keep versions only by its existing limits: 200 versions, 4 GB, and pinned versions. This removes the failure and the code behind it, but a future "undo this change" feature would have to bring the records back.
- **Keep them but let a new record replace an old one with the same number.** This is a one-line change: drop the existence check, since the write already replaces the file safely. A leftover record from a crashed turn belongs to an edit whose chat history never reached disk, so nothing loses anything. It costs nothing and keeps the option of using records later, but the design stays as it is.

My pick is to remove them if you have no planned use for them, and otherwise replace on collision. Either way the counter stays as it is and nothing new is added. Which do you want?

The current rewind feature doesn't depend on this, right? I'm a little bit confused what you mean by it's just for bookkeeping. You said that one place is still using it. Can you tell me what that place really does?
I'll check the rewind code and read the cleanup function in full before answering.

content.text:
No, the rewind features don't depend on these files. And the one place that reads them adds almost nothing, because a second mechanism already protects nearly everything they protect. I checked this on jusprin-dev.

**How the rewind features find their versions.** None of them read the `operations/` folder.
- **"Revert to here" on a change in a chat.** Each saved version's manifest records the number of the last change logged before it was saved. The button matches the chat's change list against the project's list of saved versions by that number (ShellController.cpp, around line 514), then restores that version.
- **Resuming an earlier chat.** The chat's saved checkpoint, stored in the project document, names its version, and the app restores that one.
- **File > Version history.** This reads the list of saved versions directly.

**What the one reader does.** It's the cleanup that runs after a save, `ProjectVersionStore::prune`.
- If a project has more than 200 saved versions or uses more than 4 GB, the cleanup deletes the oldest versions until it's under both limits.
- It never deletes three kinds of version:
  - the current one;
  - any version listed in the project's `pins.json`;
  - any version that an operation record names as the "before" or "after" of an edit.
- If everything left is protected, it stops and lets the project stay over the limit.

So the records are only extra "don't delete this version" markers.

**What those markers add on top of the pins:**
- **The "before" version of an AI edit is already pinned.** When an edit starts, the app saves and adds the current version to `pins.json` (`ProjectAutosave::pin_current`). The record protects it a second time.
- **The "after" version of a chat edit doesn't exist.** Inside a chat turn, no save happens after each edit, so the record's "after" is empty. The save at the end of the turn is pinned separately: in the reproduction project, `pins.json` lists all three of its versions.
- **The one real difference is edits from an outside MCP client,** such as Cursor or Claude talking to JusPrin, made while no chat turn is running. There the record's "after" is the version saved right after the edit. These records are the only thing protecting that version, so without them it could be deleted once the project passes 200 versions, like any ordinary autosave.

So inside chat turns, the files that just broke saving protect nothing the pins don't already protect. Outside chat turns, they keep a few extra versions from ever being cleaned up.

That makes the case for removing them stronger than I put it before. Removing them deletes the record writing, the existence check and that loop in the cleanup. Nothing the person can see changes, except that an outside client's edit results become ordinary versions that cleanup can delete. The only reason to keep them is a feature you have planned that reads them; I found none in the code or my notes.

**Decision needed: should I remove the operation records entirely?** The alternative is to keep them and let a new record overwrite an old one with the same number, which is a one-line change that keeps the design as it is. My pick is removal, unless you have a planned use for them. Should I remove them?
remove them. but do a theorough regression testing

=== check-for-running-ninja-before-nohup-build.md
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: a697178b-3815-42ff-b8cb-a240eb240688
  modified: 2026-10-21T19:02:35.660Z
---

On 2026-10-21 Kenneth's Mac ran at load average 32 on 12 cores for over an hour. The cause was one Claude session (the "Show MCP edits without an agent" worktree session) that launched four `nohup cmake --build … --config Release` runs between 10:56 and 11:05 into the same build dir (`.claude/worktrees/mcp-external-edits/build/arm64`), three with identical target sets. Each ninja spawned ~12 clang jobs, so 56 clang processes fought over 12 cores and every build crawled. The session had gone idle at 11:13 with its work already committed, and the builds kept running as orphans (parent pid 1) because of nohup.

**Why:** a nohup'd build survives the Bash tool timeout (see [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]]), so re-launching "the build" after each timeout adds a build instead of resuming one. ninja does not lock the build dir; concurrent instances just duplicate work and thrash.

**How to apply:**
- Before any `nohup cmake --build`, run `pgrep -fl 'ninja -f' ` and `lsof -a -d cwd -p <pid>`; if a ninja already has that build dir as cwd, tail its log instead of starting another.
- Never launch the same target set twice; wait on the saved PID with `kill -0` (see [[pgrep-wait-loop-matches-itself]]).
- Before ending a turn with the task done, kill builds you started that nobody will read (`pkill -P <ninja pid>; kill <ninja pid>`), or say in the recap that one is still running and why.
- To find who owns a stray build: the ninja's stdout path (`lsof -p <pid> -d 1`) contains the Claude Code session id; `ps -o args= -p $(pgrep -f -- "--resume=<id>")` shows the app session's side-session-notes path.
=== pkill-cmake-build-leaves-ninja.md
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 63cd6f14-4717-4149-ae93-daff41a73f76
  modified: 2026-10-21T19:12:06.265Z
---

On 2026-10-21 Kenneth found 4 Release builds and 56 clang processes on 12 cores, all mine, in one worktree. Every ninja ran at its default -j (cores + 2), so 4 × 14 = 56. He pointed out that the orphaned processes were the smaller problem. The bigger one was that I put that many builds there at all.

What I did wrong, in order of weight:
1. I treated builds as free on a machine other sessions build on too. I never passed `-j`. I saw load 33, then 76, and started more builds anyway.
2. I restarted the build three times to change its target list or to slip in a small target. Each restart cost a full set of jobs. Waiting for the running build and adding targets afterwards cost nothing.
3. I went against the brief ("reuse the existing build; another session may be building") by configuring a fresh full-app build for an optional live check.
4. I blamed the slowness on "other sessions" without counting my own processes. That is the plausible-story-instead-of-checking failure from CLAUDE.md.
5. Mechanism: `pkill -f "cmake --build <dir>"` kills only the wrapper. Its `ninja -C <dir>` child keeps compiling as an orphan. I never checked that a stop had worked.

**Why:** the machine is shared. My extra jobs slow every other session, and two ninjas in one build dir can leave its records inconsistent.

**How to apply:**
- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. Cap jobs with `-- -j4` (fewer when load is above the core count).
- Decide the full target list once. Never restart a build to change it.
- Run one build per dir as its own process group (`set -m`, then kill with `kill -- -<pgid>`). After any stop, confirm with `pgrep -fl "ninja.*<dir>"`.
- Ask before a full-app build that the task did not require.

Related: [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
=== background-bash-timeout-kills-builds.md
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

edits do not add versions.
Conversations with each chat's intent and plan, audit, and completed print
records remain in the current document; restoring a model marks the active
chat's plan for reassessment. Region descriptions follow the model: each
version records the list it was saved with, and restoring it brings that list
back. Restoring a model does not undo physical prints or change
global printer facts. Agent
mutations save and pin their actual
before-state, then link an after-version and outcome in an operation record.

## Storage and recovery contract

The restoration rules above describe ordinary Version history. **Restore and
resume** is a separate chat transition. Each chat owns its print's purpose and
plan; the project's current ones are the active chat's. A chat's checkpoint
holds a model-version reference and a structured setup summary of the moment
it was left. Browsing an older chat does not change the working project.
Resuming it saves and pins the outgoing state, restores the model with its
region descriptions, and activates that chat, whose intent and plan never left
it, only after the new document is durable. Other conversations, audit and print
records, and global printer facts remain. This does not add a full project-
document copy to model versions or make document edits create model versions.
Ordinary Version history remains model-only and does not activate an older
chat. An interrupted chat transition leaves a durable pending marker and
blocks that managed project for explicit recovery on restart.

Each model version has Orca backup-format metadata and a manifest of object
resources. It has no copy of the project document. Unchanged object resources are referenced rather
than serialized again. Changed objects are serialized with Orca's split-model
writer into immutable ZIP resources. A renamed object can reuse its resource;
materialization relabels its entry for Orca's native restore loader. Metadata
and each resource are checked for required entries and geometry. The live
Orca backup directory and an imported source file are never version-store
dependencies.

All project records advance one `current-state.json` document without creating
a model version. The document is atomically replaced after 1.5 seconds without
a change, or within 15 seconds during a continuous stream. Agent and project
boundaries wait for the write. Attachments are written once before their
document references become durable; operation records linking before/after
versions are committed once at the operation boundary. A model checkpoint
ensures the current document is durable before it publishes a new `HEAD`.

## Save classification

The autosave controller observes two independent kinds of change. Native
geometry, transforms, paint, plates, and effective project settings can change

=== workspace-harness-never-post-inits-on-mac.md
  type: project
  originSessionId: ed4bbcf2-a467-44f4-bceb-b20f93cd25d8
  modified: 2026-09-17T16:28:53.409Z
---

Found 2026-09-17 while fixing the journey-tools branch (merged to jusprin-newui as 35eb1b4a59).

`tests/workspace/real_adapter_harness.cpp` does its work in one synchronous run. On macOS, Orca adds each web view's script handler from a CallAfter (`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/WebView.cpp`) that runs a script and waits on the page in a nested event loop. In this harness the first one never returns, so `is_adding_script_handler()` stays true, the later views pile up in the static `g_delay_webviews`, and `post_init` (gated on that flag in `GUI_App.cpp`) never runs, even if the harness waits for it (it times out at 180 s).

Closing the main frame ends that wait; the deferred view setup (use-after-free on destroyed views) and then `post_init` (on a destroyed frame) run and segfault (exit 139) after `HARNESS RESULT PASS`. The harness therefore closes the frame only when `post_initialized()` (true on Windows, where the handler is added synchronously) and otherwise calls `ExitMainLoop()`.

**Why:** a Windows fix switched the exit to `Close(true)` and made every macOS run crash; an Orca-side fix (drop destroyed views from `g_delay_webviews`) removed only one of the two crashes.

**How to apply:** if the workspace harness crashes on exit, look here first; don't make it wait for post_init. The shell harness is unaffected because its checks are asynchronous. Related: [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]], [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]].
=== printer-live-harness-lessons.md
  type: project
  originSessionId: 54c192d0-38b5-4a46-8894-652694e43240
  modified: 2026-09-23T22:16:03.023Z
---

Lessons from driving the printer chat through `--printer-live` with the live model and the fake Bambu printer:

- **A reply's later lines have no `HARNESS LIVE` prefix.** A `Choices:` line sits on its own log line, so `grep "HARNESS LIVE"` hides it. On 2026-09-23 this produced a wrong report that the model never offered choices. Grep `^Choices:` separately.
- **A failed run keeps its data dir, with the API key in it.** The harness prints `HARNESS DATA DIR kept for inspection: /var/folders/.../jusprin-shell-*`. Delete the dir your own run printed, by that path. Do not sweep every `jusprin-shell-*` holding a key: another session may be running the harness in the same checkout, and on 2026-09-23 a sweep deleted a live instance's data dir.
- **Re-selecting the selected Bambu LAN printer deselects it.** DevManager's "same lan machine" path disconnects and reconnects, and GUI_App's local-connect handler (CallAfter) then sees the lost status and calls `set_selected_machine("")` after the reconnect. The connection reports "The selected printer changed". `OrcaPrinterBackend::connect_printer` now deselects and re-selects on the next event turn. The fake printer auto-selects itself when discovered, so the first connect always hits this.
- **Close OrcaSlicer's printer list (GuideFrame) only after its page loads.** It installs its web page's script handler from a CallAfter that waits on the page; `EndModal` before the load leaves that wait hanging on a hidden view, and the app freezes with no window. On 2026-09-23 this was first blamed on the product and "fixed" with a deferral, then traced to the test and reverted. Wait for `!is_adding_script_handler()`, a non-busy page and a URL, as the old `setup_manual` check did.
- **Open the panel through `ShellController::open_printer_conversation`** in live tests; `PrinterPanel::open` skips the full-window layout.
- **The model's reliability is measured, not assumed.** gpt-5.4-mini saved changes without waiting for yes in 6 of 10 runs, even with an explicit "ask, then stop" prompt. Count across several runs before calling prompt wording fixed.

See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]].

**2026-10-21, opens ignored since 2026-09-29:** `ShellController::open_printer_conversation` returns without opening while a task chat is open (guard from bb29582ff7), and `PrinterPanel::close` finishes in a CallAfter that clears that flag. The live script (written 2026-09-18) opened new chats while one was open or straight after a close, so those opens were silently ignored: the "Change" session kept the earlier Add thread, and a reopen right after a close was torn down by the late close (`--printer-live` 15 failures). Fixed in the add-printer-popup worktree (uncommitted): `live_show` closes an open chat and queues the open with CallAfter, and every "open:" step waits for `IsShown()`. `--printer-setup` gained `verify_printer_chat_reopens_fresh` (close, wait for Home, reopen, thread empty). Not a product bug: Home only returns after the close finishes.
**Queue order trap (2026-10-21):** PrinterPanel::close finishes via the panel's own CallAfter; an open queued with wxGetApp().CallAfter can run first (separate queues, no order) and is refused. Queue with live_panel()->CallAfter.
=== test-datadir-hides-orca-and-v1.md
  type: project
  originSessionId: 0bd9fd0b-1fd6-4ed7-9e9b-89af62d57bfb
  modified: 2026-11-07T18:04:39.693Z
---

2026-11-07 Kenneth ran first launch with `--datadir /tmp/JusPrin2-stg` and a pre-written JusPrin2.conf, pressed "Just slice for now", and got the manual printer form instead of the OrcaSlicer import screen. Then OrcaImporter looked for OrcaSlicer beside the data folder, so a /tmp data folder found none.

Since d289298950 / 2ccfeb0a28 on jusprin-newui-integration:
- First launch finds OrcaSlicer and v1 in their default folders, whatever `--datadir` says. `JUSPRIN_SERVER_URL` names the server, so no pre-written conf is needed.
- `JUSPRIN_ORCA_DATADIR` names another OrcaSlicer folder ("" = none).
- There is no v1 variable: Kenneth had JUSPRIN_V1_DATADIR removed ("tell the main sessino to remove it"). To start as a new person on a Mac with v1, launch with `HOME` pointed at an empty folder, and set `JUSPRIN_ORCA_DATADIR` to the real OrcaSlicer folder. To test the v1 import from a fixture, put it at `<fake HOME>/Library/Application Support/JusPrin`.
- The v1 import runs only when the data folder has no JusPrin2.conf; harnesses write one, so they never read v1.

**Why:** a test setup that hides OrcaSlicer or v1 looks like a product bug in the first-run flow.

**How to apply:** use the commands in agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md, "First launch against a staging server". Don't re-add a v1 folder variable without asking Kenneth. Related: [[first-run-flow-sequence]], [[live-checks-can-run-on-local-gateway]].

After that I moved to the JusPrin issues: JUSPRIN-APP-J, the Windows divide crash, and JUSPRIN-APP-K, the "operation version record already exists" save failure.
   - **"Reproduce on the mac first."** Done. K was reproduced on macOS with a real chat turn in the installed 2.0.0 app.
   - **"Can you crystallize the nature of the problem? I'm a little bit worried that the original design was too complex for the problem, and you're just adding more complexity..."** Answered. I withdrew the counter-repair proposal and proposed removing the records or overwriting on collision.

   - **"remove them. but do a theorough regression testing"**. This is the current task: remove the per-edit operation records and run thorough regression tests.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **JusPrin managed project store** (ProjectVersionStore):
     - versions/ (each manifest has changeSeq), HEAD, pins.json, current-state.json (the project document, with counters.nextAction).
     - operations/<action_id>.json: the removed per-edit records.
     - prune(200 versions, 4 GB) protects HEAD, pins and, formerly, the operation records.
   - **Action numbers:**
     - ToolExecutionCoordinator::submit gives every tool call an id from ProjectStateDocument::allocate_action_id (t-N).
     - Inside a model turn, the first edit pins (pin_current → save_now plus pin). Later edits reuse m_turn_before_version, and the turn end saves.
   - **Rewind paths:**
     - "Revert to here" maps change seq to version via history() (ShellController revert_to_here).
     - Resume uses the chat checkpoint versionId.
     - Version history uses history().
     - None of them read operations/.
   - **Releases 2.0.0 and 2.0.1 recreate the folder on open:** create_and_lock runs `create_directories(operations)` whenever a project is opened. So downgrading after the folder is removed is safe.
   - **Release vs RelWithDebInfo builds:**
     - In the release build, agent_busy/busy() are inlined, so they can't be forced with lldb.
     - The worktree RelWithDebInfo build is -O0, so file:line breakpoints work.
   - **Driving the app without screen control:**
     - lldb runjs.sh evaluates JS in the agent WKWebView. It uses the textarea[aria-label="Message AI"] native value setter plus an input event, then clicks button[aria-label="Send message"].
     - MCP is driven via tests/mcp/probe.py call() with mcp.json from the datadir.
   - **Worktree build recipe:** /Applications/CMake.app cmake, single CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH to deps, llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib, BUILD_TESTS=ON, -j6/-j8, nohup with logs in the scratchpad.

content.text:
I removed the per-edit operation records and tested the change, and nothing new broke. JusPrin no longer writes a file under `operations/` for each AI edit, so the "operation version record already exists" save error (Sentry JUSPRIN-APP-K) can no longer happen. Nothing is committed yet. The change is uncommitted on branch `claude/drop-operation-records` in the worktree `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/drop-operation-records`.

**What changed** (8 files, 22 lines added, 71 removed):
- **Version store** (`ProjectVersionStore.cpp`): it no longer writes operation records or creates the `operations/` folder. Version cleanup now keeps only the current version and pinned versions.
- **Opening a project:** when a project made by 2.0.0 or 2.0.1 opens, the old `operations/` folder is deleted, since nothing reads it.
- **After an AI edit** (`ShellController.cpp`): outside a chat turn, an AI edit just saves the project. Inside a turn, the save at the end of the turn covers all of that turn's edits, the same as before.
- **Tests and doc:** the tests and the autosave design doc were updated to match.

**Automated tests.** I ran each suite on the new build and on an unchanged build of the same commit, so I could tell new failures from old ones:
- **Unit tests:** all pass (201, 46 and 664 cases).
- **Workspace harness:** the new and changed version-history checks pass, including the ones that open projects saved by 2.0.0. The only 2 failures also fail on the unchanged build: a second added model gets dropped, and adding a model isn't counted as an edit.
- **Shell harness:** the autosave, reopen, blank-project, chat-restore, file-opening, storage-failure and MCP modes all pass.
  - The default mode gives 637 passes and 1 failure, on the check that the filament chat header has no hide-panel button. The unchanged build hangs at that same step.
  - The printer-setup mode gives the same 2 failures as the unchanged build, both on the "save before" path of the nozzle panel.
  - The task-chat mode hangs at the same step in both builds, and the fresh-example mode passes and then crashes on exit in both.

**Real app on my Mac:**
- A project saved by 2.0.0 with three old records opened fine, and its `operations/` folder was removed.
- **The original bug:** I ran a chat turn that made two cuts and killed the app at the end of the turn. After a relaunch, the next chat cut saved normally with no error. This is the case that threw the error before.
- **Revert to here:** this still works. It took the plate from 3 objects back to 2 and saved a new version.
- **Downgrade:** released 2.0.0 opened a project saved by the new build. It recreated its own folder, and an edit there saved fine.

I didn't then reopen that downgraded project in the new build. It's the same as the first check above: a project with 2.0.0 records opening in the new build.

**Cleanup:** I deleted the scratch data folders that held a copy of the sign-in key, the harness data folders my runs left behind, and the unchanged-build worktree. The only worktree left is the one above.

**Still open after this lands:** mark JUSPRIN-APP-K resolved in Sentry. JUSPRIN-APP-J, the Windows divide crash that triggered this, still needs a Windows reproduction.

Should I commit this on `claude/drop-operation-records` and merge it into `jusprin-dev`, or only commit it for now?
land it as one commint on jusprin-dev.
